A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WO-learner research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated proofs and experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic CATE experiments, semi-synthetic MIMIC-III evaluation, LSTM ablations, and factual outcome prediction results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds a controlled nuisance-misspecification experiment in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The WO weight construction, pseudo-outcomes, population and empirical losses, Algorithm 1, and transformer/LSTM implementations are retained. The added analyses use the existing learning procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four synthetic settings, semi-synthetic MIMIC-III CATE task, and real-world factual prediction task. The new sensitivity experiment reuses the low-overlap dataset and perturbs internal nuisance estimates without adding a population, domain, or data-input scenario.

E2.justification: Table 4 removes HA from the semi-synthetic comparison, leaving RA, IPW, DR, IVW, and WO. HA remains in other experiments. No newly cited method becomes an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: New Appendix F fixes the overlap parameter at 3.5, adds response-nuisance biases from 0 to 1 in increments of 0.1, and retrains the final-stage estimator while holding other nuisance components fixed. Existing experimental settings, metrics, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a focused sensitivity test measuring how systematic response-function estimation bias propagates to CATE error. The existing LSTM robustness experiment is moved from v1 Appendix D into Section 5, without new ablation results.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use five seeds and retain the same mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting. Figure 7 adds uncertainty bars for the new analysis but introduces no new statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New Figure 7 reports CATE RMSE rising from approximately 0.076 at zero injected bias to 0.110 at bias 1. Table 4 deletes HA's results of 0.11 ± 0.00, 0.19 ± 0.02, and 0.24 ± 0.03 for horizons 2–4. Retained benchmark scores and relocated LSTM results are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix C.4 introduces bounded conditional outcome-variance assumptions and Lemmas C.13–C.15 on DR variance inflation and bounded variance of an overlap-rescaled pseudo-outcome. The derivation explicitly treats the single-step case; the longitudinal extension is asserted. Original proofs are retained as C.1–C.3. Section 3 also narrows the formal treatment domain from a binary vector to a binary scalar.

C1.justification: The abstract and three introductory contributions retain the same claims about overlap weighting, Neyman-orthogonality, model independence, and empirical advantages. The expanded conclusion restates these existing contributions.

C2.justification: New limitations and Appendices A–B explain that WO is not doubly robust, identify accurate-nuisance and strong-overlap settings where simpler learners may suffice, and discuss the practical meaning of identification assumptions. Appendix G expands the factual prediction experiment's interpretation as a diagnostic, building on v1's existing warning that this is not the causal estimation task.

D1.justification: Appendix F documents the additive corruption formula and the freezing/retraining steps needed to reproduce the new sensitivity analysis. Existing architecture descriptions, hyperparameters, data-generation instructions, hardware, runtime, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including Frauen et al. (2025b), Ma et al. (2025), Melnychuk et al. (2026), Pearl (2009), and Poinsot et al. (2025). It expands positioning against propensity clipping and explains the IVW versus IVW-DR terminology, while retaining the original research gap.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, main section sequence, and most existing prose remain stable. Local explanations and the conclusion expand, discussion appendices are added, the LSTM subsection moves into the main text, and the header changes from preprint to conference publication.

P2.justification: v2 adds sensitivity Figure 7, relocates the unchanged LSTM table from Appendix D to main-text Table 5, removes Table 4's HA row, and enlarges Figure 3. Existing graphics and tables otherwise mainly undergo reflow and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The controlled nuisance-corruption experiment and explicit guidance about WO's lack of double robustness and favorable operating conditions add useful validation and qualifications absent from v1. These are limited gains: the new variance derivation explicitly covers only the single-step, rescaled-DR case. Table 4 also drops HA without updating the retained 28.5% improvement at horizon 4, which no longer matches the displayed best baseline.
